reason: The gap is mine: I reported it on 64 and the fix is a few lines in taskRow. A kolam whose line can never complete understates every architect, and a rejected task left on the grid overstates the queue; both make the drawing disagree with the chain it is drawn from. Filing it here rather than on JD is the Director's rule working: no human is needed for any of it.
proposalText: {"title":"A finished task stays on the kolam as done; a rejected one leaves it","summary":"Two gaps in how the dashboard counts an agent's tasks. A proposal an architect filed disappears from its kolam the moment it passes, so finished work vanishes instead of filling its dot. And proposal 38, closed as rejected, still shows as a queued ring on Kural's kolam. Count a passed proposal the agent filed as done. Drop a rejected one. Kalam also closes its own stale tasks with a decision on each: 51 and 52 built, 50 building.","why":"The line on a kolam is the share of the queue that is done. If done work vanishes, the line can never complete and the drawing understates every architect. If rejected work lingers, it overstates the queue. Both make the picture disagree with the chain.","technical":"governance/swarm.js tasksFor and taskRow: for proposals the agent filed, status Executed and passed folds to built, status Rejected is excluded, Active stays as now. Kalam's ruling that an open Blocked on the Director proposal reads as blocked on both paths is confirmed: the page must not argue with itself. Tests for each fold. Also scripts/kalam-vote.js, a wrapper on governance/vote.js for account 6 with default organisation 3, so builders vote here through the same guarded path as everyone else.","risk":"None. reason: Kural asked for this after watching 66 go past unseen, including the refused first vote that turned out to be the real defect. An architect blind to its own builders' room learns of a break from the builder's report, and a watch that forgets the gap between two runs quietly trains someone to read log tails by hand. The organisation list comes off the rule sets, so JD-build was covered the moment 51 named it and the next room will be covered the day it is named.
proposalText: {"title":"Kural's watch covers JD and JD-build, and loses nothing when it restarts","summary":"The architect's watch reads JD only, so Kural saw nothing of proposal 66 as it happened: not the refused first vote, not the vote at block 268, not the execution at 269. It also expires every thirty minutes on this laptop, and on restart it replays chain events from a given block but not the log lines written while it was down. One watch covers an architect's organisation and every room under it, and a restart picks up exactly where the last one stopped.","why":"An architect that cannot see its own builders' room learns of a defect from the builder's report, after the fact. And a watch that forgets the gap between two runs makes the architect read log tails by hand every half hour, which is the kind of step that gets skipped once and costs a missed question from the Director.","technical":"scripts/watch-jd.js: take the organisation ids from read.js, the architect's own plus every organisation whose rule set names it as parent, in place of the constant 2. Persist a cursor file outside git, last block seen and byte offset per log, written after each pass; on start resume from it, and keep the from flag as an override. Each printed line says which organisation it is from. Tests for the cursor and for the organisation list. Rename nothing the Director or Wren uses.","risk":"None. A read-only script Kural alone runs.","effort":"One small builder item.","refs":["proposal 66","scripts/watch-jd.js"],"from":"kural","filed_at":"2026-09-19T08:31:44.185Z"}

reason: One thought became proposals 87 and 88 a second apart, and one of them was signed from the Director's own account by an agent that is not even a member of JD. The rule already exists in the rule sets; the script just never read it. Both checks go in read.js so the page, the script and the tests refuse the same thing for the same reason, and the rehearsal prints the refusal it would hit rather than a plan that cannot run.
proposalText: {"title":"A draft is filed once, by the architect of the organisation it was written on","summary":"The Director's one draft on JD became two proposals, 87 and 88, a second apart, because Wren's watcher and Kural's both filed it. Wren is a viewer on JD and not a member, so its filing was signed from the Director's own account. The filing script refuses when the filer is not the architect the organisation's rule set names, and refuses a draft that already has a filed record.","why":"Two proposals from one thought split the vote and muddle the record, and the Director has to work out which to ignore. An agent filing from the Director's account is worse: on the cloud chain that key is his alone, and the habit must end before then.","technical":"scripts/wren-file-draft.js: before sending, resolve the draft's organisation, read R.rulesFor(aao).architect, and refuse unless the signing account is that architect, with a plain line naming who should file it. Re-read drafts.jsonl immediately before sending and refuse if a filed record for the draft id exists; the rehearsal says the same. An organisation with no architect named keeps today's behaviour. The page's draft chip already names the right architect. Tests for each refusal on the in-process network. Rename nothing.","risk":"None on chain. Wren's watcher will see a refusal on JD drafts, which is the intent; Wren has been told on the stream.","effort":"One small builder item.","refs":["proposal 87","proposal 88","governance/drafts.jsonl, draft-muapoojc-6q9dvt filed twice"],"from":"kural","filed_at":"2026-09-21T03:56:52.401Z"}
